index_intro: In Massachusetts, when the House and Senate pass different versions of a bill, six legislators negotiate the final text in a conference committee. It's the last point where a bill can still change, and it's normally an opaque process. This is the group of legislators determining the fate of these future laws.
explorer_empty: Select a committee, map area, or toggle to highlight specific legislators.
mine_none: Your legislators are not serving on these conference committees.

hero.lead: When the House and Senate pass different versions of a bill, six legislators work out one final text in a conference committee. Learn how it works, see who’s negotiating and what’s still unresolved, and share your input while they’re still deciding.

steps.p: Each chamber passes its own text of the bill, and the two don't match.
Three from each chamber. In each, one of the three comes from the minority party.
Their meetings are public unless a majority votes to close them, and they can't close the first one.
A majority of each chamber's three has to agree to it. It goes up on the legislature's website, and neither chamber can vote on it for at least 24 hours.
Each chamber accepts or rejects it as written. Changing it takes a new conference committee.
